paragraphs: Hertford is in Hertfordshire, so children in care in the town are looked after by Hertfordshire County Council's fostering service, shown above alongside the independent agencies that take enquiries from the town. The council is part of Foster East, the regional hub that runs its information sessions, and its recruitment line is 0800 917 0925.

The council asks for carers for several kinds of fostering. Short-term care can be anything from an overnight or weekend stay to around two years while plans are made. Emergency carers take children for about ten days at short notice and receive a retainer of £75 a day whether or not a child is with them. Long-term care is usually for children aged seven and over, sleepover carers offer at least one weekend a month or time in the school holidays, and some carers look after separated migrant children, who are usually teenagers. NEST fostering supports children moving out of residential care, with a skills payment of £1,500 a week; it needs a full-time carer at home, a spare bedroom and no children under 16 in the household.

The council says it takes four to eight months from first enquiry to approval. The route runs from a home visit through checks, references and Skills to Foster training to an assessment with a social worker and a fostering panel, and people with relevant experience may be fast-tracked. Once approved, carers get a buddy, core training, a supervising social worker who visits monthly, a duty team on weekdays and out-of-hours support seven days a week. The council's online information evenings run from 7pm to 8.30pm, and its events page lists the next one on Thursday 10 December 2026.

For what the council pays, the need for carers for teenagers and the wider county, see our Hertfordshire page. A good first step is to speak to the council and two or three of the services above, and compare their training and support.
